test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e. **'Leaving'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3 is: **'leaving'**
 
• In this context, **"leaving"** is the best choice.
 
• The sentence reads: "In fact, water falling on 93% of Switzerland ultimately passes through at least one electric power plant before even leaving the country."
 
• **This implies **that before the water exits Switzerland's borders, it passes through at least one electric power plant.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: * 'In Switzerland these glacial meltwaters are used for hydropower. In fact, water falling on 93% of Switzerland ultimately passes through at least one electric power plant before even **leaving **the country. So one consequence is that melting glaciers help to (4) __________ for low rainfall in times of drought, filling reservoirs to supply the nation's (5) __________ supply.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are not the correct answer:
 
 
• **'Throwing' - **This verb does not fit the context of water naturally flowing or being conducted through a system.
 
• **'Catching' -** Again, this verb is not suitable here as it suggests an action usually performed by a person or a mechanism designed to "catch" something, which is not the case in this context.
 
• **'Sieving' -** This term generally refers to the process of separating or filtering solids from a mixture using a tool called a sieve. However, it's not an appropriate term to describe water exiting a country's borders.
